note:
15 y/o F. CC: cough, congestion x4d.
HPI: dry cough, nasal congestion, mild sore throat. No fever, no SOB. Mother at bedside; pt provides her own history.
PMH: none. Meds: none. NKDA.
Vitals: T 98.9, HR 82, RR 16, SpO2 99%.
Exam: nasal mucosa boggy, OP mildly erythematous, lungs CTAB.
A/P: Common cold (viral URI). Supportive care, honey for cough, guaifenesin OTC. Return or go to ED if trouble breathing or fever beyond 3 days.
label_note: Common cold is minor; the teen gives her own history; ED line is a precaution.

note:
34M. CC: R ankle injury.
HPI: inverted ankle stepping off a curb 3h ago, unable to bear weight at the scene.
PMH: none.
Exam: swelling and tenderness at the posterior edge of the lateral malleolus; Ottawa positive.
XR R ankle 3 views ordered; radiology report reviewed: no fracture, soft tissue swelling.
A/P: R ankle sprain, moderate. Air-cast brace, crutches, ibuprofen OTC, RICE. Ortho f/u if not improving in 2 wks.
label_note: One test ordered and its report reviewed counts once.

note:
41F, CC dysuria x2d.
HPI: frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort. Denies fever, flank pain, vaginal sx. One UTI last year; reviewed records sent from her gynecologist's office: E. coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin.
UA dip ordered: + LE, + nitrite. Urine hCG ordered: negative.
A/P: acute cystitis, uncomplicated. Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x5d prescribed. RTC if fever or flank pain.
label_note: External records + 2 tests = 3 category-1 items; data and risk moderate; undercoded.

note:
52F, new lump in the L armpit for 3 weeks, not tender, no fever, no weight loss.
Exam: 2.5 cm firm, fixed node L axilla, breasts without masses.
She is uninsured and cannot afford an ultrasound, so I could not order imaging today; workup is significantly limited by cost.
A/P: L axillary mass, undiagnosed, uncertain prognosis. Diagnosis limited by social determinants of health (no insurance). Referred to the county charity care program for imaging and biopsy; social work referral placed.
label_note: Undiagnosed problem + care significantly limited by social determinants.

note:
63M fell on an outstretched R hand yesterday. Mild swelling at the wrist, full grip strength, snuffbox nontender.
XR R wrist 3 views ordered (my interpretation billed separately): no fracture.
A/P: R wrist sprain. Wrist splint, acetaminophen OTC, ice, recheck in 1 week if still sore.
label_note: A test whose interpretation the clinician bills separately is not counted; overcoded.

note:
38M with sudden severe L flank pain radiating to the groin for 3 hours, nausea, no fever. First episode.
UA ordered: large blood, no nitrites.
Morphine 4 mg IM given in clinic for pain, with relief.
A/P: L flank pain with hematuria, suspected ureteral stone, undiagnosed, uncertain prognosis. Outpatient CT abdomen and pelvis stone protocol ordered for today. Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily prescribed, ondansetron for nausea. ED if fever or uncontrolled pain.
label_note: IM morphine is a parenteral controlled substance (high risk), but only risk is high; overcoded.

note:
29F, two complaints today. 1) Sunburn on the face and shoulders after a beach day, no blisters. 2) Scraped her L elbow on concrete yesterday, small superficial abrasion, clean.
Vitals normal.
A/P: 1) mild sunburn; 2) superficial elbow abrasion. Aloe gel and ibuprofen OTC; abrasion cleaned and covered.
label_note: Two minor problems = low problems; OTC = low risk.

note:
4 y/o F with barky cough since last night, hoarse voice, low-grade fever. History from mother; the patient is 4 and cannot describe her symptoms.
Exam: no stridor at rest, no retractions, SpO2 98%.
A/P: mild croup. Dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg PO given in clinic. Cool mist, fluids.
label_note: Mild croup is acute uncomplicated; historian = limited data; prescription drug given in clinic; overcoded.

note:
60M here for refills; PCP retired. HTN: BP 126/78 on losartan 50 mg, stable. DM2: home fasting sugars 100-120 on metformin, stable. Hyperlipidemia: on atorvastatin 20 mg, no side effects, stable.
A/P: hypertension, type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia, all stable. Losartan, metformin and atorvastatin refilled for 90 days; establish with a new PCP.
label_note: Two or more stable chronic illnesses + prescription drug management.

note:
76F brought by her daughter for new confusion since this morning. History obtained from the daughter because the patient is confused and cannot give a reliable history. Fever 102.1, HR 118, BP 92/58.
UA ordered: positive nitrites, many WBCs. Fingerstick glucose ordered: 142.
A/P: suspected urosepsis with acute confusion and hypotension. EMS called for transfer to the ED for admission.
label_note: Historian (confused adult) + 2 tests = category 1 at moderate; threat to life + hospitalization.

note:
47M. CC: cough x 8 days.
PMH (carried forward from prior visit): HTN, DM2, hyperlipidemia; not addressed today, managed by PCP.
HPI: productive cough after a cold, no fever, no SOB, nonsmoker.
Exam: scattered rhonchi that clear with cough, SpO2 98%.
A/P: acute bronchitis. Benzonatate 100 mg TID prn prescribed, fluids, honey.
label_note: Chronic problems listed but not addressed do not count; overcoded.

note:
6 y/o M with sore throat and fever to 101 since yesterday. Father provides the history because the patient is 6 and cannot give a reliable timeline.
Exam: tonsillar exudate, tender anterior nodes.
Rapid strep ordered: positive.
A/P: strep pharyngitis. Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day for 10 days prescribed; may return to school after 12 hours of antibiotics.
label_note: Historian = limited data; acute uncomplicated + prescription.

note:
68F with COPD, followed by pulmonology. 4 days of fever 101.4, productive cough, more short of breath than usual. SpO2 93%.
Chest X-ray ordered; my read: RLL infiltrate; radiology read pending.
Discussed with her pulmonologist, Dr. Iyer, by phone: agrees with outpatient treatment.
A/P: community-acquired pneumonia, outpatient-appropriate. Amoxicillin-clavulanate and azithromycin prescribed; recheck in 48 hours.
label_note: Interpretation + discussion = extensive data, but only data is high; overcoded.

note:
58M with known heart failure, ankles more swollen for 1 week and weight up 4 kg, mild breathlessness on stairs. No chest pain. SpO2 95%, mild bibasilar crackles, no distress.
A/P: chronic heart failure with exacerbation, mild. Furosemide increased from 20 mg to 40 mg daily; daily weights; cardiology follow-up this week.
label_note: Chronic illness with exacerbation + dose change.

note:
33M stung by a bee 20 minutes ago, now throat tightness, hives, wheezing, BP 88/54.
Epinephrine 0.3 mg IM given immediately.
A/P: anaphylaxis. EMS called for emergency transfer to the ED; observed until EMS arrival.
label_note: Threat to life + decision regarding hospitalization; undercoded.

note:
25M with a red, watery R eye for 2 days after a cold, no pain, vision normal, no contacts.
Exam: conjunctival injection with watery discharge, cornea clear, preauricular node.
A/P: viral conjunctivitis. Cool compresses, artificial tears OTC, hand hygiene; contagious for about a week.
label_note: Acute uncomplicated + OTC = low; undercoded.

note:
39F with 5 loose stools since yesterday after a restaurant meal, mild cramps, no blood, no fever, drinking well.
Exam: abdomen soft, mild diffuse tenderness, moist mucous membranes.
A/P: acute gastroenteritis, uncomplicated. Oral rehydration, loperamide OTC as needed.
label_note: Acute uncomplicated + OTC.

note:
31F with neck pain after a low-speed rear-end collision yesterday. No numbness, no weakness, full range of motion with discomfort. Meets Canadian C-spine rule criteria for no imaging, so no X-ray ordered.
A/P: acute cervical strain. Ibuprofen OTC, heat, gentle stretching.
label_note: Imaging considered and not ordered is not counted.

note:
22F with asthma, severe attack since this afternoon. SpO2 88%, speaking in single words, tight air movement. Not improving after 2 DuoNeb treatments in clinic.
A/P: severe asthma exacerbation, not responding to treatment. Prednisolone 60 mg PO given. EMS called for transfer to the ED for admission.
label_note: Chronic illness with severe exacerbation + hospitalization.

note:
15 y/o M with sudden severe L testicular pain for 2 hours, vomiting once. He gives his own history.
Exam: high-riding, very tender L testis, absent cremasteric reflex.
A/P: suspected testicular torsion. Sent to the emergency department immediately for emergency ultrasound and urology evaluation; parents notified.
label_note: Threat to bodily function + escalation to emergency care; undercoded.

note:
70M with gout, painful swollen R knee since yesterday, same as prior flares. Also has type 2 diabetes, stable on metformin; steroids avoided today because of the diabetes. Kidney function normal last month per PCP.
A/P: 1) acute gout flare; 2) type 2 diabetes, stable, which changed the choice of treatment. Colchicine prescribed; metformin continued.
label_note: Chronic illness with exacerbation (and a stable chronic illness addressed) + prescription; undercoded.

note:
44F with facial pressure, purulent nasal discharge and congestion for 12 days, not improving. No fever, no eye swelling.
A/P: acute bacterial sinusitis. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg BID for 7 days prescribed, saline rinses.
label_note: Acute uncomplicated + prescription.

note:
3 y/o M vomiting since this morning, 3 episodes, one loose stool, still wetting diapers. History from mother because the patient is 3 and cannot describe his symptoms.
Exam: playful, moist mucous membranes, abdomen soft.
Ondansetron 2 mg ODT given in clinic; passed an oral fluid challenge.
A/P: acute gastroenteritis, well hydrated. Oral rehydration at home.
label_note: Acute uncomplicated; historian; prescription drug in clinic; overcoded.

note:
49M with low back pain for 3 days, now unable to urinate since this morning and numbness in the groin and inner thighs.
Exam: reduced sensation in the saddle area, weak ankle plantar flexion bilaterally.
A/P: suspected cauda equina syndrome. Sent to the emergency department now for emergency MRI and neurosurgery evaluation.
label_note: Threat to bodily function + escalation to emergency care.
